tagline: An eastern border province next to Cambodia, with Rong Kluea Market, Khmer temples, hills, and waterfalls
introHtml:
Sa Kaeo is an eastern border province that sits right against Cambodia. For most people the first thing that comes to mind is Rong Kluea Market in Aranyaprathet, a huge border market where shoppers spend the whole day picking through secondhand clothes and cheap goods. It's right by the Khlong Luek border crossing that leads over to Poipet on the Cambodian side.

Outside Sa Kaeo town there's plenty to see. Prasat Sdok Kok Thom is the largest Khmer stone temple in the eastern region; Khao Chakan is a hill with caves and clouds of bats that pour out at dusk; Pang Sida National Park has waterfalls and butterflies; and Lalu in Tap Phraya district is an eroded-earth landscape carved into pillars by water. It's a town people often stop at on the way to Cambodia, or come to for quiet nature and Khmer ruins.
bestTime: November–February, cool and pleasant — good for walking Rong Kluea Market, visiting the temples, and heading into the forest at Pang Sida. In the rainy season the waterfalls at Pang Sida are at their fullest.

highlights.name: Rong Kluea Market, Aranyaprathet
highlights.blurb: A huge border market by the Khlong Luek crossing where people spend all day digging through secondhand clothes, bags, and cheap finds. It's the first thing most people picture when they think of Sa Kaeo.

highlights.name: Prasat Sdok Kok Thom
highlights.blurb: The largest Khmer stone temple in eastern Thailand, restored to look its best. A must-stop for anyone into history wanting to learn about Khmer civilization.

highlights.name: Khao Chakan
highlights.blurb: A limestone hill with caves, a temple, and millions of bats that stream out of the caves at dusk. A nature spot close to Sa Kaeo town.

highlights.name: Pang Sida National Park
highlights.blurb: The Sa Kaeo side of the Dong Phaya Yen–Khao Yai World Heritage forest, with Pang Sida Waterfall, Pha Takhian Waterfall, and butterfly season in early rainy season.

highlights.name: Lalu, Tap Phraya
highlights.blurb: An earthen landscape eroded by water and wind into pillars and cliffs, a bit like Phae Mueang Phi. It's out near Tap Phraya district, and you can tour it by farm tractor.

highlights.name: Khlong Luek–Poipet border crossing
highlights.blurb: A busy Thai–Cambodia crossing right next to Rong Kluea Market, the main route for travelers heading to Siem Reap and Angkor Wat.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Sa Kaeo eats mostly Isan-style — som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, and sticky rice, easy to find all over town and at the markets.

foodScene.name: Noodles and street food in Aranyaprathet
foodScene.note: Around Rong Kluea Market and in Aran town there are noodle shops, rice-and-curry stalls, and street snacks to grab while you shop.

foodScene.name: Cambodian-style border food
foodScene.note: Near the border you'll find Khmer-influenced dishes mixed in — clear-broth noodles, sweets, and snacks that carry flavors from the Poipet side.

foodScene.name: Wang Nam Yen melons and fruit
foodScene.note: Wang Nam Yen and Wang Sombun districts grow melons and other fruit, with farms where you can buy fresh and pick up processed treats as gifts.

foodScene.name: Mu krata
foodScene.note: A go-to dinner for locals and groups of friends — plenty of grill-your-own pork places at easygoing prices.

foodScene.name: Freshwater fish and tiny shrimp
foodScene.note: The reservoirs and canals supply fresh freshwater fish and tiny shrimp, served boiled, fried, or in spicy salads at local restaurants.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town
foodScene.note: Sa Kaeo town and Aranyaprathet have new cafes and coffee shops opening up — handy for a break between sights.

attractions.name: Rong Kluea Market
attractions.blurb: A huge border market by the Khlong Luek crossing where you can dig through secondhand clothes and cheap goods all day. A must-stop for anyone visiting Sa Kaeo.

attractions.name: Prasat Sdok Kok Thom
attractions.blurb: The largest Khmer stone temple in eastern Thailand, beautifully restored, with an information center telling the story of Khmer civilization in the area.

attractions.name: Prasat Khao Noi Si Chomphu
attractions.blurb: An old Khmer temple on a hill near Aranyaprathet. Climb the stairs to see the ruins and the views all around.

attractions.name: Pang Sida National Park
attractions.blurb: A World Heritage forest with Pang Sida Waterfall, Pha Takhian Waterfall, hiking trails, and butterfly season in early rainy season.

attractions.name: Khao Chakan
attractions.blurb: A limestone hill with caves, a temple, and clouds of bats streaming out at dusk. A nature spot close to town.

attractions.name: Lalu
attractions.blurb: An earthen landscape eroded into pillars and cliffs, a bit like Phae Mueang Phi, out near Tap Phraya district. You can tour it by farm tractor.

attractions.name: Tap Phraya National Park
attractions.blurb: Forest along the Banthat mountain range against the border, with viewpoints, quiet nature, and several Khmer temples nearby.

attractions.name: Sa Kaeo–Sa Khwan
attractions.blurb: The pair of ancient ponds that gave the province its name, right in town — a spot locals use for history and a bit of rest.
